assertions.name: the_two_weights_have_DIFFERENT_SUPPORT
assertions.source: At n=6 the Markov weight y_lambda vanishes on 7 of 11 partitions (every lambda with more than 2 rows -- the SU(2) row cap) while the Plancherel weight the consumer uses is nonzero on all 11. They are not two weightings of one sum; they are sums over DIFFERENT INDEX SETS, and no lambda-independent rescaling relates them.

assertions.name: markov_and_plancherel_weights_differ
assertions.source: y_lambda != dim_q^2/[n]_q! per partition at n=6, q0 — so the consumer's weight is not the Markov weight

assertions.name: markov_trace_of_identity_is_one
assertions.source: SUM_lam y_lam chi^lam(1) = 1 exactly -- y_lam IS a normalised Markov trace, confirming the weights were read correctly

assertions.name: consumer_weighting_of_identity_is_NOT_one
assertions.source: SUM_lam (dim_q^2/[n]_q!) chi^lam(1) = 11.139447540, not 1. A Markov trace sends the identity to 1 by definition, so the quantity the consumer labels tr_M is not a Markov trace -- this is a fact about the object, independent of any convention choice.

description: Asks whether the quantity `beta_ew_delta_I_321_and_wedderburn.py` labels a 'Wedderburn-weighted Markov trace' -- SUM_lam (dim_q^2/[n]_q!) chi^lam -- equals the Markov trace SUM_lam y_lam chi_lam that AGENTS.md gives as this framework's canonical Frobenius pairing. Follow-on from bean qou-oots, which named this file as the one live non-harness consumer of the superseded Plancherel weight. The prior question is not WHICH Plancherel family it should use but whether a Plancherel weight belongs there at all, since the Markov trace is defined with the Ocneanu weights y_lam. Reports the per-partition weight ratio, the two traces of the same character vector, whether the ratio is lambda-INDEPENDENT (which decides whether the file's six cot(theta_W) candidates -- all same-n ratios -- move at all, as against only its label being wrong), and the q -> 1 control where the register says the families coincide.

T1_per_partition_n6.note: y_lambda is the Ocneanu/Markov weight (SU(2) member, convention D) as the corpus computes it; w_plancherel is the weight the consumer uses.

T3_is_the_reweighting_lambda_independent.CAVEAT: Computed only where BOTH weights are nonzero, so it UNDERSTATES the difference -- the partitions where y_lambda vanishes are excluded, and those are the point. A weight that is zero where the other is positive cannot be reached by ANY lambda-independent rescaling, so the invariance question is already settled NO by the support difference.
T3_is_the_reweighting_lambda_independent.consequence: The consumer reports SIX cot(theta_W) candidates and every one is a ratio of w-weighted quantities at the SAME n. A lambda-independent reweighting cancels exactly from all of them, so if this is True the label is wrong but the numbers stand; if False the reported candidates are not invariant under using the weight the name claims.

T2_traces_of_the_same_character_vector.chi_used: chi^lam(identity) = f^lam — a fixed, exactly-known vector, so any difference is attributable to the WEIGHTS alone

T4_control_at_q_to_1.reading: If y_lambda is STILL zero on the same partitions as q -> 1, the support difference is NOT a q-deformation effect -- it is the SU(2) row cap, a statement about N that survives the classical limit. The register's 'the families coincide at q = 1' then does not extend to y_lambda at N = 2.
T4_control_at_q_to_1.note: The notation register says the three partition-weight families coincide at q = 1. If the spread here does NOT collapse toward 1, the difference measured at q0 is not the q-deformation and a different explanation is needed.
